question: A school office wants to bring Claude into its existing parental-enquiry workflow. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Map the workflow as it runs now; run it alongside the old way; choose one step to hand over; compare the two and then decide
B) Choose one step to hand over; map the workflow as it runs now; compare the two and then decide; run it alongside the old way
C) Run it alongside the old way; compare the two and then decide; map the workflow as it runs now; choose one step to hand over
D) Map the workflow as it runs now; choose one step to hand over; run it alongside the old way; compare the two and then decide
correct_answers: D) Map the workflow as it runs now; choose one step to hand over; run it alongside the old way; compare the two and then decide
explanations: Running the new way before deciding which step it replaces leaves the parallel run undirected, and the choice is then made after the evidence.
Choosing a step before the workflow is mapped means the choice is guesswork, and comparing before running has nothing to compare.
Running and comparing before the workflow is understood produces a result nobody can interpret, and the mapping arrives too late to matter.
Correct. Map what exists, choose one step, run the new way in parallel so nothing is lost, then compare before committing. Parallel running is what makes the comparison safe.
